questions.question: A rectangular prism (a cuboid) measures 8 cm long, 5 cm wide and 3 cm high. You are opening it out flat to draw its net with every dimension labelled. How many rectangles must the net have, and how do their sizes pair up?
options: 6 rectangles, forming 3 matching pairs
8 rectangles, forming 4 matching pairs
5 rectangles, forming 2 pairs and 1 single
4 rectangles, forming 2 matching pairs
questions.explain: Opening a cuboid flat gives one rectangle per face, and a cuboid has 6 faces in 3 matching pairs: 8 by 5, 8 by 3, and 5 by 3. The common trap is counting only the faces you can see from one side and drawing 4 or 5.

questions.question: A triangular prism has two identical triangular ends and is 12 cm long. You are drawing its net flat on paper with all dimensions labelled. Which shapes must the net contain?
options: 2 triangles and 4 rectangles, 6 shapes in all
2 triangles and 3 rectangles, 5 shapes in all
3 triangles and 3 rectangles, 6 shapes in all
2 triangles and 2 rectangles, 4 shapes in all
questions.explain: Roll a triangular prism flat: the two triangular ends, plus one rectangle for each of the triangle's 3 sides, gives 5 shapes. The usual slip is copying a shoebox and drawing 6 faces.

questions.question: A cylinder has radius 4 cm and height 10 cm. Its net is made of two circles and one rectangle. Using π ≈ 3.14, what size must the rectangle be?
options: 8 cm long and 10 cm tall
12.6 cm long and 10 cm tall
25.1 cm long and 10 cm tall
4 cm long and 10 cm tall
questions.explain: The rectangle wraps once all the way around the circle, so its length is the circumference: 2 × 3.14 × 4 = 25.1 cm, and its other side is the height, 10 cm. The classic trap is using the diameter, 8 cm, which is only the distance straight across.

questions.question: Yuki is drawing the net of a soup can, a cylinder with radius 3 cm and height 11 cm. Which pieces must her net contain?
options: One circle of radius 3 cm and one rectangle
Three circles of radius 3 cm and one rectangle
Two circles of radius 3 cm and two rectangles
Two circles of radius 3 cm and one rectangle
questions.explain: A cylinder net needs one circle for each flat end plus one rectangle for the curved surface: two circles and one rectangle. Forgetting the second circle folds up into a can with no lid.

questions.question: Maya is cutting a paper label that wraps right around a cylindrical candle for a craft fair in Kelowna. The candle has diameter 14 cm and height 9 cm. On the net, that label is the rectangle. Using π ≈ 22/7, what size should she cut it?
options: 44 cm by 9 cm
88 cm by 9 cm
14 cm by 9 cm
22 cm by 9 cm
questions.explain: The label goes all the way around, so its length is the circumference: 22/7 × 14 = 44 cm, and its height stays 9 cm. Cutting it 14 cm long uses the diameter, the distance straight across rather than around.

questions.question: A triangular prism has ends that are right triangles with sides 3 cm, 4 cm and 5 cm, and the prism is 10 cm long. On its net, every rectangle shares the 10 cm measurement. What are those rectangles?
options: 3 cm × 10 cm, 4 cm × 10 cm and 4 cm × 10 cm
3 cm × 10 cm, 4 cm × 10 cm and 5 cm × 10 cm
5 cm × 10 cm, 5 cm × 10 cm and 5 cm × 10 cm
a single rectangle measuring 12 cm × 10 cm
questions.explain: Each rectangle has one side equal to the prism's length, 10 cm, and the other equal to one side of the triangle, giving 3 × 10, 4 × 10 and 5 × 10. Every triangle side needs its own labelled face, so it cannot be shown as one 12 cm strip.

questions.question: On the net of a rectangular prism, one rectangle is 9 cm by 4 cm, and the rectangle joined along its 4 cm edge is 4 cm by 6 cm. Every face size appears exactly twice. What are the remaining two rectangles?
options: Two rectangles, each 9 cm by 4 cm
Two rectangles, each 4 cm by 6 cm
Two rectangles, each 9 cm by 6 cm
Two rectangles, each 9 cm by 9 cm
questions.explain: The three face sizes come from pairing up the three dimensions 9 cm, 4 cm and 6 cm; 9-by-4 and 4-by-6 are already drawn, so the missing pair is 9 by 6. The trap is repeating a size you already have instead of pairing the two dimensions left over.

questions.question: A cylinder net is drawn as two circles plus a rectangle that is 31.4 cm long and 12 cm tall. Using π ≈ 3.14, what is the radius of each circle?
options: Radius 10.0 cm
Radius 2.5 cm
Radius 15.7 cm
Radius 5.0 cm
questions.explain: The rectangle's length is the circumference, so 2 × 3.14 × r = 31.4, giving r = 5 cm. Dividing 31.4 by 3.14 gives the diameter, 10 cm, which still has to be halved — and 31.4 itself is never the diameter.

questions.question: Priya draws a net for a cylindrical thermos with diameter 8 cm and height 20 cm. She draws two circles of radius 4 cm and a rectangle 8 cm by 20 cm. Using π ≈ 3.14, what is wrong with her net?
options: The rectangle should be 25.1 cm by 20 cm, to match the circumference.
The circles should have radius 8 cm, since the rectangle's side is the radius.
The rectangle should be 12.6 cm by 20 cm, since half of it wraps around.
The net should have just one circle, since the two ends are identical.
questions.explain: The rectangle has to wrap all the way around, so its length is the circumference, 3.14 × 8 = 25.1 cm, not the 8 cm measured straight across. Priya used the diameter; the circumference is always a bit more than three times that.

questions.question: Devi is drawing a net for a tent shaped like a triangular prism. The triangular end has a base of 4 m, two equal sloping sides, and a perimeter of 9 m. The tent is 6 m long. What are the three rectangles on her net?
options: 6 m × 9 m, a single wrap-around rectangle
6 m × 4 m, 6 m × 4 m and 6 m × 2.5 m
questions.explain: First find the sloping sides: 9 − 4 = 5 m shared by two equal sides, so each is 2.5 m. Then each rectangle is 6 m by one triangle side, giving 6 × 4, 6 × 2.5 and 6 × 2.5 — three separate faces, not one long strip.

questions.question: A cylindrical rain barrel at a community garden in Surrey has radius 20 cm and height 50 cm. Ravi draws its net with all dimensions labelled. Using π ≈ 3.14, how do the two sides of the rectangle compare?
options: The rectangle is 10 cm shorter than it is tall
The rectangle is 12.8 cm longer than it is tall
The rectangle is 75.6 cm longer than it is tall
The rectangle is 125.6 cm longer than it is tall
questions.explain: The rectangle's length is the circumference, 2 × 3.14 × 20 = 125.6 cm, and its height is 50 cm, so it is 125.6 − 50 = 75.6 cm longer than tall. Using the diameter, 40 cm, would wrongly make the rectangle shorter than the barrel is tall.

questions.question: Leo draws a net for a chocolate box shaped like a triangular prism, 20 cm long. He draws 2 triangles and 4 rectangles, saying a prism has 6 faces just like a shoebox. What should you tell him?
options: A triangular prism has 4 faces; the two triangles share one rectangle.
A triangular prism has 6 faces; his rectangles are just the wrong size.
A triangular prism has 5 faces; it needs 1 triangle, as the ends match.
A triangular prism has 5 faces; it needs 3 rectangles, one per side.
questions.explain: A triangular prism has 5 faces: 2 triangles plus one rectangle for each of the triangle's 3 sides. Only a box-shaped prism has 6, so count the sides of the end shape to know how many rectangles the net needs.
